equation_request.abstract: A quantum algorithm is presented for the simulation of arbitrary Markovian dynamics of a qubit, described by a semigroup of single qubit quantum channels $\{T_{t}\}$ specified by a generator $\mathcal{L}$. This algorithm requires only $\mathcal{O}\big((||\mathcal{L}||_{(1\rightarrow 1)}t)^{3/2}/\epsilon^{1/2}\big)$ single qubit and CNOT gates and approximates the channel $T_{t}=e^{t\mathcal{L}}$ up to chosen accuracy $\epsilon$. Inspired by developments in Hamiltonian simulation, a decomposition and recombination technique is utilised which allows for the exploitation of recently developed methods for the approximation of arbitrary single-qubit channels. In particular, as a result of these methods the algorithm requires only a single ancilla qubit, the minimal possible dilation for a non-unitary single-qubit quantum channel.

specification.problem: Approximate a single-qubit Markovian channel T_t=e^{tL} generated by a Lindbladian L to accuracy epsilon, using single-qubit and CNOT gates with one ancilla qubit.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Only the abstract-stated target channel, the stated gate-count scaling, and a generic background Trotter-like decomposition and recombination skeleton with a one-ancilla Stinespring dilation. The specific channel-approximation method, the decomposition of L and the recombination rule are outside scope.

equations.label: Semigroup slicing and decomposition
equations.description: Generic product-formula skeleton consistent with the decompose-and-recombine idea; not the paper's actual decomposition.
equations.justification: Standard Lie-Trotter structure for semigroups; the abstract only says a decomposition and recombination technique is used.

equations.label: One-ancilla dilation
equations.description: Single-qubit channel realised by a unitary on system plus one ancilla qubit.
equations.justification: Stinespring dilation. Qubit channels with at most 2 Kraus operators need one ancilla; the abstract states one ancilla suffices.
assumptions: The ancilla is reset or fresh for each channel application

specification.initial_state: System in an arbitrary input state rho; ancilla in |0>.

steps.description: Fix the target T_t=e^{tL}, the accuracy epsilon and the norm.
Decompose the evolution into short-time pieces and recombine them as a product (the paper's specific decomposition is not given).
Implement each piece as a single-qubit channel via a one-ancilla dilation compiled to single-qubit and CNOT gates, using the unspecified channel approximation methods.

assumptions: Diamond norm is assumed for epsilon.
The product-formula skeleton is generic background, not the paper's method.
Ancilla reuse or reset between slices is assumed.
